details:
How Does TERRASHIFT Work?

TERRASHIFT provides an interactive environment where users can explore geographic locations, examine environmental conditions, and investigate changes over time.

The platform follows five main stages:

1. Explore Earth

Users navigate an interactive 3D globe or 2D map, search for geographic locations, and select areas of interest, including cities, districts, regions, and countries.

2. Access Scientific Data

The platform connects to scientific information services, including NASA POWER for meteorological variables and NASA GIBS for supported satellite visualization layers.

Users can explore environmental information such as air temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation, subject to the availability, spatial resolution, and temporal coverage of the underlying datasets.

3. Investigate Surface Changes

TERRASHIFT incorporates SAR analysis workflows to compare radar observations acquired on different dates.

These workflows can identify candidate changes in radar backscatter and support the investigation of surface dynamics. The platform distinguishes preliminary detections from scientifically confirmed events to avoid misleading interpretations.

4. Visualize and Understand Results

Environmental information is presented through interactive maps, temporal charts, indicators, scientific explanations, and supporting evidence.

Users can inspect data sources, observation periods, measurement units, geographic coverage, and methodological limitations.

5. Support Future Preparedness

The architecture is designed to evolve toward validated predictive models, environmental risk assessment, and early-action planning tools.

These advanced capabilities remain part of the project's development roadmap and are not presented as fully operational forecasting or official warning systems.

3. Benefits and Expected Impact

TERRASHIFT aims to make Earth observation more useful and accessible to society.

Environmental understanding: Users can investigate environmental conditions and changes through understandable geographic representations rather than interpreting complex satellite files independently.

Scientific accessibility: Students, researchers, local communities, and public institutions can explore environmental information without requiring advanced expertise in remote sensing.

Evidence-based decision-making: Scientific provenance, temporal comparisons, and explicit uncertainty help users distinguish observed information from preliminary analysis or future projections.

Environmental resilience: The platform can support future applications involving flood monitoring, forest change, climate variability, agricultural conditions, and territorial preparedness.

Global accessibility: Its geographic exploration experience is designed for international use, while the availability of individual datasets and analyses depends on the selected location and scientific source.

Our long-term vision is to help communities and institutions recognize environmental changes earlier, understand their potential implications, and make better-informed decisions.

4. Technologies and Development Tools

TERRASHIFT was developed using a modern, modular software architecture.

Frontend and Visualization

  • Next.js, React, and TypeScript for the interactive web application.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive interface development.
  • MapLibre GL and supporting mapping technologies for geographic visualization.
  • Interactive 2D maps, 3D globe exploration, temporal charts, and scientific information panels.
  • Spanish and English localization to improve international accessibility.

Backend and Data Processing

  • Python and FastAPI for scientific services and API development.
  • PostgreSQL with PostGIS for geospatial information management.
  • Redis for caching and supporting asynchronous operations.
  • Celery workers for background processing.
  • MinIO and S3-compatible storage concepts for scientific artifacts and datasets.
  • Docker and Docker Compose for service isolation and reproducible local environments.

Scientific and Geospatial Technologies

  • NASA–ISRO NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar data.
  • NASA POWER meteorological datasets.
  • NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS).
  • Python-based geospatial and raster-processing workflows.
  • Scientific metadata, evidence records, and SHA-256 checksums for data traceability.

Development and Quality Assurance

The team used Git-based development workflows, automated frontend and backend testing, API contract validation, and Chromium-based end-to-end testing.

The project was developed using conventional software development hardware and containerized environments rather than specialized satellite-reception equipment.

5. What Makes TERRASHIFT Creative and Innovative?

TERRASHIFT is designed to go beyond displaying satellite imagery.

Its innovation lies in bringing several complementary capabilities into one accessible planetary exploration experience.

A unified Earth exploration environment

Instead of requiring users to switch between multiple specialized scientific platforms, TERRASHIFT brings geographic exploration, meteorological context, SAR-based investigations, and scientific evidence into a shared interface.

Science explained in natural language

The system emphasizes understandable explanations so that nontechnical users can interpret environmental information without losing essential scientific context.

A visual connection between location and time

Users can examine places geographically and compare information across available periods, supporting a clearer understanding of how environmental conditions evolve.

Scientific transparency by design

TERRASHIFT explicitly differentiates satellite observations, gridded meteorological estimates, preliminary change candidates, and future predictive capabilities.

Its evidence-oriented architecture supports source attribution, reproducibility, and communication of scientific limitations.

A foundation for planetary intelligence

The platform is designed to progressively integrate additional environmental datasets, validated machine learning models, and decision-support capabilities without fragmenting the user experience.

6. Important Factors Considered by Our Team

Throughout development, our team prioritized several principles:

Scientific reliability: Environmental measurements and satellite-derived findings must be linked to authentic sources. Preliminary observations must not be presented as confirmed disasters or verified physical changes.

Data quality and uncertainty: Spatial resolution, temporal coverage, missing values, and methodological limitations must be communicated clearly.

Accessibility and usability: The platform should be understandable to researchers, students, local authorities, and members of the public. A bilingual, responsive interface helps support this goal.

Geographic scalability: The architecture should allow users to investigate different territories without relying exclusively on predefined demonstration locations.

Security and privacy: Public geographic exploration must remain separate from protected user operations, with appropriate access controls, validation, and request limits.

Modular engineering: Scientific processing, data acquisition, visualization, and future machine learning functions should remain independently maintainable while sharing common data contracts.

Responsible communication: TERRASHIFT does not claim to issue official emergency alerts. Its purpose is to support scientific understanding and complement information from competent authorities.

Long-term sustainability: The system is designed with reusable components and scalable data-processing approaches to support future expansion.

7. Project Development Status and Future Vision

TERRASHIFT currently includes an interactive geographic interface, 2D and 3D exploration, bilingual navigation, public environmental data queries, temporal visualization, and exploratory scientific workflows based on Earth observation data.

Initial scientific investigations have included SAR-based change analysis in Peru and water-observation analysis in Mozambique.

The platform also incorporates evidence tracking and quality controls to distinguish preliminary scientific findings from validated conclusions.

The current release is a working prototype undergoing final deployment and integration validation. Global forecasting, advanced machine learning inference, comprehensive environmental risk modeling, and official operational warning capabilities are not yet complete.

Our future goal is to develop TERRASHIFT into an integrated planetary intelligence platform that connects Earth observation, scientifically validated analysis, forecasting, and preparedness.

8. Conclusion

TERRASHIFT seeks to bridge the gap between observing Earth and understanding what those observations mean for people.

By combining NASA Earth observation resources, SAR analysis, interactive mapping, environmental information, and a transparent scientific approach, our project demonstrates how modern software engineering can make complex planetary data more accessible.

We envision a future where communities, researchers, and decision-makers can better understand environmental change and use trustworthy scientific information to support resilience.

TERRASHIFT — Observe Earth. Understand Change. Anticipate Tomorrow.
